newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Comalco slips after smelting report.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Comalco slips after smelting report.

text.p: Shares of aluminium producer Comalco Ltd were weaker on Monday following a newspaper report that the company had abandoned plans to expand its smelting division.
At 1.25 p.m. (0225 GMT), Comalco shares were 16 cents weaker at A$6.70 on turnover of 58,900 shares.
"It (the newspaper report) maybe the reason for the fall, but on such low volume it's very hard to tell," said Eric Gale, director of instotutions at broker Ord Minnett.
Gale said it was not surprising that Comalco would be looking at a phase of consolidation for its smelting operations after that division's recent expansion.
The Sydney Morning Herald newspaper report said the smelting division had told its workforce that it had abandoned a growth strategy after a six-month review of operations.
The report said the company was concerned about the deteriorating cost position of their smelting investment.
Comalco owns all of the Bell Bay smelter in Tasmania and 79.36 percent of the Tiwai Point smelter, New Zealand, and 50 percent of Boyne Island, Queensland.
Comalco is 67 percent owned by RTZ-CRA group.
